buy.title: Buying African government securities: what, who, how
buy.lede: For banks, funds, insurers, corporate treasurers and individuals. Government securities are debt securities (Treasury bills and bonds), not shares: by subscribing, the investor lends to the state, which repays the face value at maturity and pays interest. The procedures below are quoted word for word from official pages. Access is never guaranteed, and nothing here is investment advice.

sim.title: What would an operation earn?
sim.lede: Pick an upcoming auction (synthetic data) or enter your own parameters. The simulator computes the price, the amount to pay, the interest and the gain net of the fees and taxes you enter. It is arithmetic, not a forecast: the rate actually obtained depends on the auction result.
sim.kind.bill: Treasury bill: discount, interest paid up front (zero-coupon)
sim.err: Check the inputs: positive amount, valid rate, term, fees and tax (tax between 0 and 100%).
sim.err.price: With this discount rate and term the price becomes zero or negative: inconsistent inputs.
sim.op.note: Inputs pre-filled from the synthetic auction ({c}, {d}). The rate is that of the previous auction of the same maturity.
sim.unit: According to BEAC, the unit face value of this security is {u}: the amount should be a multiple of it.
sim.ken: According to the Central Bank of Kenya: minimum KES 50,000 (non-competitive bid) or KES 2,000,000 (competitive bid), in denominations of KES 50,000.
sim.cpn.assume: The line's actual coupon is not available: it defaults to the yield (price at par). Change it if you know it.
sim.disclaimer: Illustrative simulation. Actual fees and taxes are not stated by official sources: the values entered are yours. Neither advice nor a guarantee of return or allotment.
sim_assume_bill: Security held to maturity, face value repaid in full.
Interest paid up front: you pay the price and receive the face value; the difference is the interest.
The rate convention and day-count basis vary by market and have not been verified for every country: use those in the auction notice.
Fees computed on face value; tax computed on gross interest. No FX or inflation.
sim_assume_bond: Bought at issue, held to maturity, one coupon per year, no accrued interest or settlement lag.
Coupons are not reinvested in the net gain; the net yield to maturity assumes reinvestment at the same rate.
Tax applied to coupons only; fees computed on face value and paid at purchase. No FX or inflation.
st.title: Diversification and cross-country cooperation
st.lede: A framework for institutional investors, intermediaries and Treasuries: how to spread risk across issuers, maturities and monetary zones, and which forms of cross-country cooperation can widen market access. This is not an investment recommendation.
strategy_levers: Spreading subscriptions across several states reduces exposure to a country-specific event (fiscal stress, auction postponed or cancelled). Limit: states in the same zone often share common shocks (commodity prices, regional liquidity).

Staggering maturities, for example 3 months, 1 year, 3 years and 5 years, smooths interest-rate and reinvestment risk: part of the portfolio matures regularly and can be reinvested at prevailing terms.

Combining the CFA franc (XOF, XAF), rand-area currencies (CMA) and national currencies changes the nature of currency risk. Limit: XOF and XAF have the same fixed parity with the euro; combining them diversifies issuer risk, not currency risk against the euro.
Combining bills (short term, discount) and bonds (periodic coupons) balances liquidity and income. Bills roll over often; bonds lock in a rate for longer but are more sensitive to rate changes.
Taking part in several auctions rather than one reduces dependence on a single date's rate: the average entry price is smoothed over time.
strategy_limits: Diversification guarantees neither a higher return nor the absence of loss. It reduces each issuer's specific risk, not the risk common to all (global rate rise, regional shock).

A higher nominal yield generally compensates for higher risk (credit, currency, liquidity, inflation). Yields of different countries cannot be compared without accounting for inflation, exchange rates and calculation conventions.
National currencies add currency risk and, depending on the country, convertibility or repatriation rules to check with the central bank.
Market data on this site is synthetic: the tool below illustrates a method and describes no real portfolio.
st.pf.title: Diversification test bench
st.pf.lede: Build a fictitious portfolio (country, maturity, weight) and look at its concentration. Rates are the latest synthetic weighted average yields from the grid; no portfolio is proposed or optimised.
st.pf.empty: Add at least one line with a positive weight.
st.r.eur: Share in CFA franc, pegged to the euro
st.r.zar: Share in rand and linked currencies (CMA)
st_pf_notes: HHI: sum of squared shares in %. 10,000 = everything in one line; the lower it is, the more spread the portfolio.
The weighted average yield ignores currency risk, inflation, fees, taxes and cross-country correlations.
st.coop.lede: Cartouche's proposals for intermediaries, investors and Treasuries, to be discussed and checked with the relevant authorities. These are interpretations, not established facts.
strategy_coop: In WAEMU as in CEMAC, several states' securities are issued on a common regional market with common rules and intermediaries. A single intermediary can therefore, in principle, carry subscriptions across several states of the zone: confirm with it.
Primary dealers and banks from different countries can team up to bid together, share issuer analysis and split allotments, widening their investor base.
Pooling savings in a fund lets small investors reach several countries despite high face values (CFA 1 million per BTA in CEMAC, according to BEAC).
Treasuries that share their calendars can avoid tapping the same investors in the same week and smooth their refinancing schedules.
Bringing central securities depositories and settlement systems closer across zones would cut the cost and delays of investing in several monetary zones.
Publishing calendars, results and rate conventions in common formats, and training local investors, broadens domestic and regional demand.
gl.title: Terms and abbreviations
gl.lede: Definitions of the market terms and acronyms used on the platform. Zone-specific definitions cite their official source where one exists.
glossary: French for auction: issuance method in which the Treasury offers an amount of securities; bids are filled in order of rate (lowest first) or price up to the amount accepted.
Autorité des Marchés Financiers de l'Union Monétaire Ouest-Africaine: regulator of the WAEMU regional financial market.
Bon Assimilable du Trésor (WAEMU): short-term debt security issued by auction; maturity under 2 years according to UMOA-Titres.
Banque Centrale des États de l'Afrique de l'Ouest: central bank of the 8 WAEMU states.
Banque des États de l'Afrique Centrale: central bank of the 6 CEMAC states.
Bourse Régionale des Valeurs Mobilières: stock exchange shared by the WAEMU states.
Bon du Trésor Assimilable (CEMAC): 13, 26 or 52 weeks, face value CFA 1 million, interest paid up front (BEAC).
Bourse des Valeurs Mobilières de l'Afrique Centrale: CEMAC regional stock exchange.
Central Bank of Kenya, which runs the auctions of Kenyan Treasury bills and bonds.
Central African Economic and Monetary Community: Cameroon, Central African Republic, Congo, Gabon, Equatorial Guinea, Chad; currency XAF.
Common Monetary Area: South Africa, Eswatini, Lesotho, Namibia; currencies linked to the South African rand.
Commission de Surveillance du Marché Financier de l'Afrique Centrale: CEMAC financial market regulator.
Periodic interest paid by a bond, expressed as a percentage of face value.
Cellule de Règlement et de Conservation des Titres: central depository of CEMAC government securities, according to BEAC.
Central Securities Depository. DhowCSD is the Central Bank of Kenya's portal to open a securities account and submit bids.
French for maturity: date the face value is repaid. Residual maturity is the time remaining until that date.
Bond issued on international markets, usually in dollars or euros, outside the issuer's domestic market.
Herfindahl-Hirschman Index: sum of squared shares (in %); 10,000 means total concentration on a single item.
French for interest paid up front (discount): the investor pays a price below face value and receives the face value at maturity.
Primary market: buying securities at issue, from the state. Secondary market: buying and selling already-issued securities between investors.
Face value: amount repaid at maturity, on which coupons are calculated.
Obligation Assimilable du Trésor (WAEMU): medium- and long-term debt security issued by auction; maturity over 3 years according to UMOA-Titres.
French for collective investment scheme (UCITS-type fund) pooling the savings of several investors.
Obligation du Trésor Assimilable (CEMAC): term of 2 years or more, face value CFA 10,000, annual interest (BEAC).
Basis point (bp): one hundredth of a percentage point, 0.01%. A move from 8.00% to 8.25% is 25 bp.
Weighted average yield: average rate of the bids accepted at an auction, weighted by the amounts accepted.
Société de Gestion et d'Intermédiation (WAEMU): licensed broker-dealer buying and selling securities for clients.
Competitive bid: the investor states the rate or price it accepts. Non-competitive bid: it accepts the rate resulting from the auction.
Spécialiste en Valeurs du Trésor (primary dealer): accredited credit institution that takes part in auctions and makes the secondary market in government securities.
Bid-to-cover ratio: total bids divided by the amount offered. Above 1, demand exceeds supply.
West African Economic and Monetary Union (WAEMU): Benin, Burkina Faso, Côte d'Ivoire, Guinea-Bissau, Mali, Niger, Senegal, Togo; currency XOF.
Regional agency that organises auctions of government securities (BAT and OAT) for the WAMU states.
ISO codes of the WAEMU (XOF) and CEMAC (XAF) CFA francs. Same fixed parity with the euro (EUR 1 = CFA 655.957), but the two currencies are not interchangeable.
Distance of a value from the mean of its history, in standard deviations.
m.title: From official publication to signal passport
m.lede: No figure is produced by a language model. Published values stay facts, derived values are calculations, and nothing mixes the two. Steps I and II arrive in phase 2; today the engine runs on synthetic data.
m.s1.p: Every day, official pages (BEAC, BCEAO, UMOA-Titres, CBK…) are checked: availability, changes, newly published documents.
m.s2.p: Auction notices and results in PDF: text, OCR, structured fields. Each document is deduplicated by fingerprint and goes through a human verification queue.
m.s3.p: Deterministic rules with explicit thresholds and neutral labels. Re-running it creates no duplicates.
m.s4.p: Facts used, calculation, rule triggered, what would invalidate the signal, and limitations. All archived for audit.

guide_steps: Choose an accredited intermediary: primary dealer (SVT), bank or SGI, or direct access where the central bank allows it (DhowCSD portal in Kenya).
Open a securities account and a cash account; provide the identification documents requested (know-your-customer).
Read the issuance calendar and the auction notice: amount offered, maturity, bid deadline (date and time), value date.
Send your order before the intermediary's internal cut-off: competitive bid (you state a rate) or non-competitive bid (you accept the rate set).
Fund the cash account for settlement on the value date.
Receive the allotment notice: the order may be filled in full, in part or not at all.
Track coupons and redemption at maturity; optionally sell the securities on the secondary market.

mk.k.note: Over the selected period. Amount allotted: sum of the published amounts (calculation). Buybacks are never added to issuance.
mk.curve.aria: Scatter of the latest weighted average yields by residual maturity, {c}: {n} points
mk.curve.note: Observed points, not joined: for each reference maturity (3 and 6 months, 1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 7, 10 and 15 years), the latest issuance auction of the last 365 days whose residual maturity is closest to it. Horizontal axis: time to maturity at settlement (maturity minus settlement), log scale. No curve is fitted or interpolated; points may come from different days. Buybacks excluded.
mk.nodata.curve: No issuance auction with a published yield in the last 365 days.
mk.nodata.period: No verified issuance auction in this period.
mk.tip.none: No verified issuance auction this month.
mk.hist.aria: Weighted average yields of issuance auctions over time, by maturity bucket, {c}: {n} points
mk.hist.note: Each point is an issuance auction (published weighted average yield), bucketed by residual maturity at settlement.
